title: List every place GREG's code starts a process, opens a connection or listens, and fail CI on any new or rewritten one until a person files it
problem: Directive section 37 says: "If consequential workers can bypass the evidence plane, treat it as a security defect." Section 67 kills architecture that "permits consequence-gate bypass". Before this unit nothing in the tree listed where greg/ and foundry/systems/ start processes, open connections or listen, so a new spawn or connection around the capability manifests, the Gate, the worker envelope or the #26 relay could be noticed only by a reviewer reading the diff. Measured at the unit's base b1950be2: a subprocess.run appended to greg/compute.py passed the existing suites (69 passed). Later the base itself added two spawns, which this branch found only when its scan ran on the merged tree: greg/licensing.py :: system_binary (bd7e3f9e, a dpkg-query run from the body's own tick) and greg/compute.py :: benchmark (#238).
founder_intent_refs: INTENT-20261028-OPUS-MAXIMUS-REISSUE (sections 37 governed observability and 67 kill criteria; also 34-36, 56 and 64)
baseline: b1950be2 (#196's head when the unit began): no inventory of effect sites; only a reviewer reading the diff could notice a new spawn, connection or listener. The PR base is now #196 at d35d92a5, which still has none.

alternatives.name: Proposed: AST inventory with pins, wrappers, path lookups and a fixed list of findings, guarded by a 117-mutant gate
alternatives.description: tests/unit/test_effect_call_allowlist.py parses greg/, foundry/systems/ and every repository module they import (328 modules on the merged tree) and finds each child process, stdlib call that starts one, outbound connection, name lookup, listener and exec/eval/runpy. tests/security/effect-call-allowlist.json lists each site by (module, qualname, callee) with a count, what serves it and a pin of the code it describes. Declared wrappers make each caller a site. path_lookups records where each program is chosen by name. FINDINGS in the test fixes which entries are body-loop findings. scripts/ci/check_effect_call_allowlist_mutants.py holds 117 mutants. No source module changes.
advantages: A new effect site fails CI with a ready-to-paste entry; it caught the base's dpkg-query spawn at merge 275e9d86 and #238's compute.benchmark spawn at merge 7f179554
15 of 15 evasion forms in the third review's probe are sites (the round-3 scanner found 0)
Re-filing a finding as allowed fails (FINDING RE-FILED); before round 4 it passed
A rewritten pinned spawn fails (PIN MISMATCH); before round 4 it passed
A new direct caller of system_binary or git_read fails (UNLISTED); before round 4 it passed

The inventory surfaced real defects for their owners: dpkg-query, bwrap and git taken from the body's ambient PATH, git_read running a repository's core.fsmonitor, the system-52 string check passed by "052", run_worker's cortex child with full network, and install_filter's find_library spawn
No source module, authority or capability changes; reverting four files removes it
disadvantages: Static: effects inside third-party libraries, python -c children, non-literal importlib or getattr, ctypes other than find_library, socket.fromfd and stdlib functions not in the table are unseen
A pin binds what runs at a site, not who reaches it: a986fc74 added a route to system_binary and the scan stayed green
Size: a 1685-line test and a 1598-line JSON; every PR that adds an effect must add and pin an entry
The mutant gate took 27m14s as one process on a shared 4-core container and is not in canonical-ci.yml
The envelope rule matches words; a justification that relies on the sandbox in other words is not held to it
alternatives.revival_evidence: Retained as proposed. Revisit if CI cost or false positives block unrelated PRs, or if runtime enforcement (below) lands.

alternatives.name: Simplest viable: round 1's scanner (callee and count only, greg/ and foundry/systems/ only)
alternatives.description: The first version at f4028f3d: an AST scan of a fixed callee table keyed by (module, qualname, callee) and a count, 67 keys, 20 mutants, no wrappers, no pins, no import following.
advantages: About 8 s per scan and 2m18s for its mutant gate
Much smaller to read and maintain
disadvantages: Round 2's 14 new source mutants all survived it: rebinding, re-export, star import, sys.modules, asyncio.subprocess, urlretrieve, open_connection, httpx2, a listener, an evaluated annotation, an opener's .open held as a value, getattr(opener, "open"), a new egress.send caller and run_isolated(isolate_network=False)
It missed 12 real sites: 4 httpx2 clients and 8 listeners
It filed memory_bytes as operator-only although the body loop reaches it, and carried a false justification for _launch
alternatives.revival_evidence: Only if the full scanner's maintenance cost is shown to exceed what it catches; the measured misses above argue against it.

alternatives.name: Strongest competing: enforce at runtime instead of listing at review time
alternatives.description: Install a CPython audit hook (sys.addaudithook) or OS confinement on the body process so that a subprocess, socket or exec event not issued through a governed path is refused.
advantages: Sees effects inside third-party libraries and dynamic forms that a static scan cannot
Blocks an effect instead of recording it
The audit hook is stdlib and already worked here as a probe: it observed find_library spawning /sbin/ldconfig -p
disadvantages: Changes the body's runtime behaviour: a source change, outside this no-source unit
Six body-loop spawns and the path lookups have no governed path yet, so enforcing today would stop the body or need exemptions that recreate the list
In-process code can still reach the OS through ctypes; an audit hook is a tripwire, not a boundary
Needs the founder's decision on what the running body may refuse
alternatives.revival_evidence: A source unit that puts the six findings and the ambient-PATH lookups behind confinement or a governed path; this inventory is the list such a unit starts from.

alternatives.name: Staged or reversible experiment: report the inventory as a warning for a period before it fails CI
alternatives.description: Run the same scan but only print new or changed sites, and measure how many real sites and false positives appear before making it blocking.
advantages: No CI friction while its noise is measured
disadvantages: A warning does not stop a bypass; the two base spawns above reached #196 with no such check in place
The measurement it would produce already exists: across four base merges and 20 clean sibling merges the scan flagged exactly two new sites, both real, and no false positive
alternatives.revival_evidence: False positives that block unrelated PRs in CI.

do_nothing_option.expected_outcome: New spawns, connections and listeners keep landing seen only by whoever reads the diff. The two base spawns this scan caught at merge time (licensing.system_binary, compute.benchmark) reached the integration line that way.
advantages: No new test, data file or mutant gate to maintain
disadvantages: Section 37's "treat it as a security defect" has no detector
Six body-loop spawns with nothing governing them, and the ambient-PATH choice of dpkg-query, bwrap and git, stay unrecorded
The git_read fsmonitor exposure and the system-52 string check stay undiscovered

The test and the JSON are large; their own self-tests and mutants are what keep them honest

pass_1.intended_outcome: Every place GREG's own Python code, and the repository modules it imports, starts a process, opens a connection, looks up a name, listens or runs code from a string is listed with what governs it. A new or rewritten one fails CI until a person reads the code and files it. A body-loop spawn that nothing governs is filed as a finding that cannot be relabelled an approval.
